incident-bot: :rotating_light: P0 — Serving runtime errors detected in eu-west cluster (autoscale thrash leading to crashloops). Alert group: runtime/cuda/oom. Root ts: 1815004321

sam (oncall): I'm on it. seeing 5xx spike on /v1/generate, latency jump to 2s -> 10s, increased pod restarts.

dino-sre: can you paste the kube events and recent HPA events? I suspect scale down -> scale up oscillation.

sam (oncall): grabbing logs now. posting top errors:
```
2026-03-15T12:05:03Z runtime: ERROR CUDA_ERROR_OUT_OF_MEMORY: failed to allocate 3.2GiB
2026-03-15T12:05:07Z runtime: INFO restarting container (exitCode=137)
2026-03-15T12:05:12Z autoscaler: scaleDown triggered (replicas 24 -> 6) due to low short-term CPU
2026-03-15T12:05:35Z autoscaler: scaleUp requested (6 -> 28) after queue length spike
2026-03-15T12:05:36Z kubelet: pod crashloopbackoff - crashCount=8
```

tara (eng-runtime): that pattern is classic thrash. autoscaler aggressive cooldown + reactive queue bursts cause nodes to be oversubscribed during scale up because startup pods try to allocate full VRAM and get OOM.

jordan (infra): showed a node-level metric: GPU memory fragmentation high on newly provisioned instances. Provisioning latency ~30s so many pods start mid-provision and attempt allocation immediately.

sam (oncall): immediate mitigation idea list: 1) pause HPA/autoscaler 2) cordon a few noisy nodes 3) scale to stable capacity to drain backlog 4) pin to smaller model variant for EU region 5) inform CS/customer. what do folks think?

dino-sre: agree. Follow order: pause autoscaler (to stop oscillation) -> set desired replicas to a conservative number -> kill crashlooping pods so new sched picks healthier nodes -> apply node taint to prevent new pods on bad nodes -> adjust startup resource requests to allow warmup step.

ops-bot: /run playbook incident/scale-stabilize v1 (dry-run)

```

kubectl annotate deployment/model-serving cluster-autoscaler.kubernetes.io/scale-down-disabled=true --overwrite

kubectl delete pod -l app=model-serving,region=eu -n prod-eu --force --grace-period=0
```
